notes: This page claims a smallest defining pair (E_0,K_0), gives a binomial degree bound, defines CM bimodules, and constructs ψ_Σ by determinant before a base-extension diagram. Check 149.N1: for the d-element subset A of the 2d-element set in the stated permutation action, g Stab(A)↦gA is well defined and bijective onto its orbit: equality of images is exactly membership of g₂⁻¹g₁ in Stab(A). The orbit is contained in the set of d-element subsets, whose cardinality is binom(2d,d). This verifies the combinatorial index bound only. The norm argument is visibly x1_Σ, with a cancelled raised Σ; it was not converted to an exponent to repair the mathematics. Check 149.N2: in the finite split-coordinate description from the stated finiteness hypothesis, 1_Σ has 1 on Σ and 0 on its nonempty CM complement. At x=1 its full-algebra norm is therefore 0, whereas the preceding determinant on t has value 1. Thus the written full-algebra norm formula fails this identity check. Refined formula 149.N3: N(1−1_Σ+x1_Σ) equals the determinant on t, since its diagonal entries are the x-coordinates on Σ and 1 on the complement, giving exactly the same product. This explicit relation explains the alternative exponent reading without changing the ink. Archive number 148.
